items.title: The Big Long? Michael Burry Closes Nasdaq-100 Short, Says His Portfolio Is Now Almost Entirely Long
items.summary: The investor who bet against the AI boom just changed course, yet he still has a target on his list. Michael Burry's new book reveals which stocks he buys, which he keeps shorting, and who he may hunt next.

items.title: Apple, Amgen Lead 5 Dow Jones Stocks Near Buy Points
items.summary: These Dow Jones components have show strong relative strength in a tricky market. Most are actionable now, including Apple stock.

items.title: OpenAI Countersues Apple, Accusing It of “Coercing and Threatening” Suppliers
items.summary: OpenAI waited until the market closed to hit back at Apple, claiming the iPhone maker leaned on shared suppliers to stall its hardware ambitions. The money at stake is tiny, but the real fight is over who gets to build the next AI device.

items.title: Apple’s COO Has Now Filed to Sell $39 Million of Stock in 3 Days
items.summary: Apple's supply chain chief just sent a second sale notice to the SEC while the stock sits at a record high. Only one of the two trades is confirmed, and the fine print shows where the shares came from and what could happen next.

items.title: Apple Is Beating the Rest of the "Magnificent Seven" in 2026. Can It Do It Again in 2027?
items.summary: Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta Platforms have pushed their free cash flow into the negative due to AI spending, while Apple has continued to generate cash.

items.title: Vanguard's Growth ETF Has 3 Stocks Making Up More Than a Third of It. Only 1 Has Held Up in the Tech Sell-Off.
items.summary: The stock that's held up best belongs to the slowest grower of the three.

items.title: OpenAI says a spy handed Apple secret plans for AI devices that could 'outcompete' the iPhone maker on its 'own turf'
items.summary: OpenAI and Apple are suing each other for stealing as the race to develop AI products fuels competition for talent and technology.

items.title: 2027 smartphone market outlook: Apple to outperform as shipments fall 5%
items.summary: Investing.com -- Global smartphone shipments are expected to decline 5% in 2027 following a projected 14% contraction in 2026, with Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) positioned to gain market share, according to Bernstein.
